subject: Operating Systems
text: What is a process in an operating system?
optionA: A program stored but not executing
optionB: An instance of a program currently executing
optionD: A collection of device drivers only
explanation: A process is an executing instance of a program, together with its execution state and allocated resources.

subject: Operating Systems
text: Which statement describes First-Come, First-Served (FCFS) scheduling?
optionA: The process with the shortest remaining time always runs first
optionB: Processes are served in arrival order
optionC: Every process receives a fixed rotating time quantum
optionD: The process with the highest priority always runs first
explanation: FCFS schedules ready processes in the order they arrive and is normally non-preemptive.

subject: Operating Systems
text: Which deadlock condition describes a circular chain in which each process waits for a resource held by the next process?
explanation: Circular wait exists when a closed chain of processes each waits for a resource held by the next process in the chain.

subject: Operating Systems
text: What is the main purpose of a semaphore?
optionB: To coordinate access to shared resources between concurrent processes or threads
optionC: To translate virtual addresses into physical addresses
explanation: A semaphore is a synchronization primitive used to control access to shared resources through wait and signal operations.

subject: Operating Systems
text: In paging, virtual memory is divided into fixed-size units called:
explanation: Paging divides virtual address space into fixed-size pages and physical memory into corresponding frames.

subject: Operating Systems
text: When does a page fault occur?
optionA: Whenever the CPU executes an arithmetic instruction
optionB: When a referenced virtual page is not currently resident in physical memory
optionC: When a process releases a semaphore
explanation: A page fault is raised when a process accesses a page that is not currently mapped to a resident physical-memory frame.

subject: Operating Systems
text: In Round Robin scheduling, what is the time quantum?
optionA: The maximum number of processes in the system
optionB: A fixed time slice allocated to a process before it is preempted
optionC: The time required to format a disk
optionD: The priority value of the process
explanation: Round Robin gives each ready process a time slice; an unfinished process returns to the ready queue when its quantum expires.

subject: Operating Systems
text: What does contiguous file allocation mean?
optionA: A file's blocks are stored in consecutive disk locations
optionB: Every file is stored in a separate partition
optionD: A file is stored only in RAM
explanation: Contiguous allocation stores a file in a sequence of adjacent disk blocks.

subject: Operating Systems
text: Which request does the Shortest Seek Time First (SSTF) disk-scheduling algorithm select next?
optionA: The request with the earliest submission timestamp
optionB: The request whose track is closest to the current disk-head position
optionC: The request with the largest file size
optionD: The request at the highest cylinder number
explanation: SSTF chooses the pending request requiring the smallest seek distance from the current head position.

subject: Operating Systems
text: What does mutual exclusion guarantee for a shared critical section?
optionA: All processes enter it at the same time
optionB: At most one participating process or thread enters it at a time
optionC: No process can ever be blocked
optionD: The critical section executes only during boot
explanation: Mutual exclusion prevents simultaneous entry into a critical section by competing processes or threads.
